description.text:
The promos of Japan's Platinum years: 51 cards, 001/DPt-P to 051/DPt-P, released from October 2008 to August 2009. The run began alongside Galactic's Conquest, the first expansion of the DPt series, when DP-P gave way to DPt-P.

Many were prizes: at Gym Challenge store tournaments, at Challenge Hiroba, at the tournaments held for the release of each new expansion, in the Pokémon Battle Tour 2009 and at the tournament that chose Japan's World Championships players. Others came from release campaigns and Special Packs for Galactic's Conquest and the sets after it, the Pokémon Daisuki Club's member ranks, the film Arceus: To a Conquering Spacetime and its Movie Commemoration Special Pack, an official Arceus deck case and Weekly Shōnen Sunday.

tell.text: A PROMO star at the bottom right, and a "/DPt-P" number

description.text:
One of five original cards of the launch campaign for Galactic's Conquest (ギンガの覇道), the first expansion of the new Pokémon Card Game DPt series, released on 10 October 2008. From that day, while stocks lasted, every two packs of Galactic's Conquest bought at once came with one of the five, Carnivine G, Manaphy, Rotom, Probopass G and Darkrai G, without a choice of which. Card shops, Pokémon Centers and the 7-Eleven, Lawson, Circle K and Sunkus convenience stores took part, except some stores, and the card came only from the shop where the packs were bought. Some shops, though no convenience stores, also gave out an SP Pokémon Secret Fun Book (SP（スペシャル）ポケモン マル秘おたのしみブック) about the expansion's new SP Pokémon.

Carnivine G is one of Team Galactic's SP Pokémon, marked G (ギンガ) after its name. Makoto Imai drew it.

It is a Supporter card of Cyrus (アカギ) that brings a Supporter, a basic Energy and a Team Galactic's Invention card from the deck to the hand. Ken Sugimori drew it.

Came with the Pokémon Card Game DPt Official Visual Book, Galactic's Conquest edition, which Media Factory published on 11 October 2008, the day after the expansion's release. The 96-page book, the first of the DPt series, showed every card of Galactic's Conquest and the Entry Pack in color, with sample decks such as a Toxicroak G, Skuntank G and Weavile G deck, and came with this holo card, drawn only for the book.

The DP visual books before it came with Lucario LV.X 004/DP-P, Garchomp LV.X 058/DP-P, Porygon-Z LV.X 075/DP-P, Heatran LV.X 092/DP-P and Drapion LV.X 123/DP-P. Toxicroak G is one of Team Galactic's SP Pokémon, marked G (ギンガ) after its name. Ryota Saito drew it.

description.text:
The third Pokémon Center 10th anniversary card. To mark ten years since the Pokémon Centers opened, all five stores, Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya, Fukuoka and Yokohama, gave it to each shopper from 14 to 28 November 2008, one per person while stocks lasted. Squirtle was picked by a vote over Meowth. Like the earlier cards' Shopping and Little Errand, its attack Souvenir Pick (おみやげえらび) brings a card from the deck: it looks at the top two and keeps one.

Pikachu came first, from 30 May 2008, in a slightly different version at each store (098 to 102/DP-P), then Charmander 124/DP-P from 22 August 2008. Bulbasaur 030/DPt-P followed from 4 April 2009, when shoppers who brought any two different cards of the four got a Pokémon Card Game coin. Yuka Morii made it.

One of the two special holo cards in the Pokémon Card Game DPt Galactic's Conquest and Bonds to the End of Time Special Pack (ギンガの覇道・時の果ての絆 スペシャルパック), which The Pokémon Company released on 1 January 2009. The pack held two boosters of Bonds to the End of Time and one of Galactic's Conquest, eleven cards each with one holo, plus Electrode G and Mismagius GL LV.X, which were always included. It followed the July 2008 special packs for Moonlit Pursuit and Dawn Dash and for Cry from the Mysterious and Temple of Anger.

Electrode G is one of Team Galactic's SP Pokémon, marked G (ギンガ) after its name. Yusuke Ishikawa drew it.

Given to every player of the Gym Challenge (ジム☆チャレンジ) tournaments that shops of the official Pokémon Card Gym network held for the release of Bonds to the End of Time (時の果ての絆), on sale from 26 December 2008. Every player got Alakazam E4 012/DPt-P and Team Galactic's Invention G-109 SP Radar 013/DPt-P, and the top finishers Luxray GL 014/DPt-P; all three carry the Gym Challenge logo in their text box.

The SP Radar trades a card from the hand back into the deck for an SP Pokémon from it. Kent Kanetsuna drew it.

Luxray GL is a Gym Leader's SP Pokémon, marked GL (ジムリーダー), one of the Gym Leaders' and Elite Four's SP Pokémon that appear in the expansion. Kouki Saitou drew it.

The card of Lucario, the "department head" (ルカリオ部長) of Pokémon Sunday (ポケモン☆サンデー), TV Tokyo's Sunday-morning Pokémon show. From the episode of 14 December 2008, the show followed the making of the card: Lucario and Robert (ロバート) visited the people who make Pokémon card illustrations in 3D computer graphics, in clay and in 2D drawing, Robert tried drawing Lucario too, and Lucario chose Mitsuhiro Arita's 2D drawing, striking its usual "Roger!" (ラジャー) pose for it.

From 17 January 2009, while stocks lasted, shops across Japan gave the card to anyone who brought one Fighting Pokémon card to trade and said the password "Roger!", one per person, with a Bonds to the End of Time fun book. The fun book points out its secrets: a P.S.C. logo in the background, the Roger pose, the Pokémon Sunday logo, and a Poké-Body also called Roger, under which players reply to each other with a hand on the chest and a "Roger!". Its attack Brick Break (かわらわり) was chosen because Lucario broke roof tiles on the show. The card can be used in official tournaments.

A reward of Pokémon Card Game Action Points (PCGアクションポイント), the points system of the official Pokémon Daisuki Club fan club, mailed to members who reached Gold Rank at 1,200 points. Members earned points by playing in official tournaments and at official gyms, among other activities, and each rank had its own rewards: Super Rank, at 3,200 points, brought Cresselia 045/DPt-P and Darkrai 046/DPt-P. The Pikachu came packed with an Upper Energy card from Bonds to the End of Time.

When the L-P promos took over, Gold Rank brought Pikachu 019/L-P instead. The points system ended on 31 August 2010. Kanako Eo drew it.

A prize for the top finishers of the tournaments held in March 2009 to launch the Beat of the Frontier expansion (フロンティアの鼓動), whose logo it carries. At the Card Get Battle version, Battle Tower 019/DPt-P came with a first win and Dragonite FB 018/DPt-P with further wins; at the version that shops ran as a Gym Challenge, every player got Battle Tower and SP Energy 020/DPt-P.

Drifblim FB is a Frontier Brain's SP Pokémon, marked FB after its name. Lee HyunJung drew it.

The fourth and last Pokémon Center 10th anniversary card. To mark ten years since the Pokémon Centers opened, all their stores gave it to each shopper from 4 to 17 April 2009, one per person while stocks lasted, and shoppers who also brought any two different cards of the four got a Pokémon Card Game coin. Like the earlier cards' attacks, its attack Present (プレゼント) brings a card from the deck, here any card on a coin flip.

Pikachu came first, from 30 May 2008, in a slightly different version at each store (098 to 102/DP-P), then Charmander 124/DP-P from 22 August and Squirtle 009/DPt-P from 14 November 2008. Yuka Morii made it.

A prize for five straight wins in the Card Get Battles at Challenge Hiroba events from May 2009. Challenge Hiroba (ポケモンチャレンジひろば) events, held in shopping malls and department stores, offered teaching corners, lotteries, free battles, trading corners and Card Get Battles (カードゲットバトル), small tournaments played until a player lost, up to five rounds. This silver Victory Medal shows Giratina and reads "For the Winner of the Pokémon Card Game" in English.

Yusuke Ishikawa drew it.

Given to participants of Challenge Hiroba events in May 2009, when the events began handing out a new promo card every month. Challenge Hiroba (ポケモンチャレンジひろば) events, held in shopping malls and department stores, offered teaching corners, lotteries, free battles, trading corners and Card Get Battles (カードゲットバトル), small tournaments played until a player lost, up to five rounds. Five straight wins in that month's Card Get Battles brought the Giratina Victory Medal 031/DPt-P.

Kagemaru Himeno drew it.

The trophy card of the final stage of the Pokémon World Championships Japan Representative Tournament (ポケモンワールドチャンピオンシップス日本代表決定大会), which chose Japan's players for the 2009 World Championships. After a first stage in all 47 prefectures from October 2008 and six regional second-stage tournaments in March and April 2009, the final stage was held at the Prince Park Tower Tokyo on 4 May 2009, for card game and video game players together.

The top finishers of both games got the card set in an acrylic plaque showing their placing, blue for the card game and red for the video game: 36 cards in all, 20 to card game players and 16 to video game players. The card reads ポケモンカードゲーム公式大会入賞カード, a placing card of an official Pokémon Card Game tournament. Ryo Ueda drew it.

Given to players of the Card Get Battles at Challenge Hiroba events from June 2009. Challenge Hiroba (ポケモンチャレンジひろば) events, held in shopping malls and department stores, offered teaching corners, lotteries, free battles, trading corners and Card Get Battles (カードゲットバトル), small tournaments played until a player lost, up to five rounds. Its text box carries an advertisement for the next expansion, Advent of Arceus (アルセウス光臨), on sale from 8 July 2009, and Porygon-Z G 035/DPt-P, given at Gym Challenge events that month, carries an Advent of Arceus banner too.

Kanako Eo drew it.

Given to players of Gym Challenge (ジム☆チャレンジ) events at shops of the official Pokémon Card Gym network from June 2009. Its text box carries a banner for the next expansion, Advent of Arceus (アルセウス光臨), released on 8 July 2009, as does Ponyta 034/DPt-P from the Challenge Hiroba events of the same month.

Porygon-Z G is one of Team Galactic's SP Pokémon, marked G (ギンガ) after its name. Nobuyuki Fujimoto drew it.

A prize for three straight wins in the Knockout Battle (ノックアウトバトル) of Pokémon Battle Tour 09. Pokémon Battle Tour 09 (ポケモンバトルツアー09) was the big Pokémon event of summer 2009, held at shops across Japan, mostly AEON group stores, on one day each between 11 July and 6 September 2009, in place of the Battle Road tournaments of earlier summers. It offered card battles, a beginners' class, a lottery and a chance to try the new Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver games. The Knockout Battle had a standard league with 60-card decks and a half league with 30-card decks, open to all ages; three straight wins in either league brought this silver Victory Medal, showing Arceus, and in the standard league the gold one too, 051/DPt-P. Everyone who took part got Mewtwo 049/DPt-P.

Yusuke Ishikawa drew it.

Given to every player of the Gym Challenge (ジム☆チャレンジ) tournaments that shops of the official Pokémon Card Gym network held in July 2009 to launch Advent of Arceus (アルセウス光臨), released on 8 July 2009. Every player got Beginning Door, some shops adding Rainbow Energy 021/DPt-P; winning players got Pichu 038/DPt-P and the top finishers Mothim 039/DPt-P. All three carry the expansion's logo on the illustration.

Beginning Door brings an Arceus from the deck to the hand. Ryo Ueda drew it.

Mitsuhiro Arita drew it.

Given to cinema-goers at the release of Arceus: To a Conquering Spacetime (アルセウス 超克の時空へ), the 2009 Pokémon film, known in English as Arceus and the Jewel of Life, which opened in Japan on 18 July 2009. Kunihiko Yuyama, the film's director, drew it.

description.text:
Came with issue 33 of Shogakukan's Weekly Shōnen Sunday (週刊少年サンデー), published on 29 July 2009, drawn for the magazine by Gosho Aoyama, the creator of Detective Conan, which has run in Weekly Shōnen Sunday since 1994. It is the official card of the Spiky-eared Pichu of that summer's Pokémon film, Arceus: To a Conquering Spacetime, which opened on 18 July 2009, and carries the film's logo.

The M (ムービー, movie) after its name marks it as one of the film's SP Pokémon, and its attack Friend Party (ともだちパーティー) puts any number of Pokémon with M in their names from the deck onto the bench.

One of the two special holo cards in the Pokémon Card Game Movie Commemoration Special Pack 2009 (映画公開記念スペシャルパック2009), released on 18 July 2009, the opening day of the Pokémon film Arceus: To a Conquering Spacetime. The pack held one booster of Advent of Arceus, eleven cards with one holo, and two Movie Commemoration Random Packs 2009 of seven cards each with one holo, plus Pikachu M LV.X and Michina Temple, which were always included. Both are credited to 2009 Pikachu Project.

Pikachu M LV.X levels up from Pikachu M; the M (ムービー, movie) marks the film's SP Pokémon, and it carries a portrait of Ash beside its SP mark.

One of the two special holo cards in the Pokémon Card Game Movie Commemoration Special Pack 2009 (映画公開記念スペシャルパック2009), released on 18 July 2009, the opening day of the Pokémon film Arceus: To a Conquering Spacetime. The pack held one booster of Advent of Arceus, eleven cards with one holo, and two Movie Commemoration Random Packs 2009 of seven cards each with one holo, plus Pikachu M LV.X and Michina Temple, which were always included. Both are credited to 2009 Pikachu Project.

Michina Temple is named after Michina, the town of the film's story, whose temple was built for Arceus. The card shows Pikachu, Piplup and Spiky-eared Pichu before it, and once in each of their turns lets each player remove two damage counters from a Pokémon with M in its name.

A reward of Pokémon Card Game Action Points (PCGアクションポイント), the points system of the official Pokémon Daisuki Club fan club: members who reached Super Rank, at 3,200 points, were mailed Cresselia 045/DPt-P and Darkrai 046/DPt-P. Members earned points by playing in official tournaments and at official gyms, among other activities; Gold Rank, at 1,200 points, brought Pikachu 016/DPt-P. When the L-P promos took over, Super Rank brought Cresselia 020/L-P and Darkrai 021/L-P instead, and the points system ended on 31 August 2010.

The two cards work as a pair. Cresselia's Poké-Body Crescent Aura (みかづきのオーラ) removes a damage counter from it at every Pokémon Checkup while Darkrai is in play, and Darkrai's Dark Aura (あんこくのオーラ) adds 20 damage to its attacks while Cresselia is. Wataru Kawahara drew both.

A reward of Pokémon Card Game Action Points (PCGアクションポイント), the points system of the official Pokémon Daisuki Club fan club: members who reached Super Rank, at 3,200 points, were mailed Cresselia 045/DPt-P and Darkrai 046/DPt-P. Members earned points by playing in official tournaments and at official gyms, among other activities; Gold Rank, at 1,200 points, brought Pikachu 016/DPt-P. When the L-P promos took over, Super Rank brought Cresselia 020/L-P and Darkrai 021/L-P instead, and the points system ended on 31 August 2010.

The two cards work as a pair. Darkrai's Poké-Body Dark Aura (あんこくのオーラ) adds 20 damage to its attacks while Cresselia is in play, and Cresselia's Crescent Aura (みかづきのオーラ) removes a damage counter from it at every Pokémon Checkup while Darkrai is. Wataru Kawahara drew both.

Given to players of the Card Get Battles at Challenge Hiroba events from August 2009, the events' new promo card that month. Challenge Hiroba (ポケモンチャレンジひろば) events, held in shopping malls and department stores, offered teaching corners, lotteries, free battles, trading corners and Card Get Battles (カードゲットバトル), small tournaments played until a player lost, up to five rounds. Earlier 2009 Challenge Hiroba cards were Chatot 032/DPt-P in May and Ponyta 034/DPt-P from June, and the Giratina Victory Medal 031/DPt-P went to players who won five Card Get Battles in a row.

Kagemaru Himeno drew it.

cards.name: アルティメットゾーン

description.text:
The launch campaign card of Advent of Arceus (アルセウス光臨), released on 8 July 2009. From that day, while stocks lasted, shops taking part gave one for every two packs of the expansion bought at once, glued into the Ultimate Zone strategy book (アルティメットゾーン激攻略BOOK), whose original comic showed how to use it to make Arceus stronger. It came only from the shop where the packs were bought.

Ultimate Zone is a Stadium with an original illustration that lets each player move Energy from Benched Pokémon to an Active Arceus as often as they like. Kent Kanetsuna drew it.

Given to everyone who took part in Pokémon Battle Tour 09, in its Battle Trial for elementary school children and younger and in its Knockout Battle alike; even players who only tried HeartGold and SoulSilver got it. Pokémon Battle Tour 09 (ポケモンバトルツアー09) was the big Pokémon event of summer 2009, held at shops across Japan, mostly AEON group stores, on one day each between 11 July and 6 September 2009, in place of the Battle Road tournaments of earlier summers. It offered card battles, a beginners' class, a lottery and a chance to try the new Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver games. Three straight Knockout Battle wins brought the Arceus Victory Medals 036/DPt-P and 051/DPt-P.

Ken Sugimori drew it.

The one new card in the Pokémon Battle Tour 09 Challenge Deck (ポケモンバトルツアー09 チャレンジデッキ), a ready-made 30-card half deck built around Fire Pokémon and sold only at the venues of Pokémon Battle Tour 09. Every other card in it was a straight reprint, with no symbol or number of the deck's own. Players without a deck of their own could use it in the tour's Battle Trial for children and in the half league of its Knockout Battle. Pokémon Battle Tour 09 (ポケモンバトルツアー09) was the big Pokémon event of summer 2009, held at shops across Japan, mostly AEON group stores, on one day each between 11 July and 6 September 2009, in place of the Battle Road tournaments of earlier summers. It offered card battles, a beginners' class, a lottery and a chance to try the new Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver games.

Wataru Kawahara drew it.

A prize for three straight wins in the standard league of the Knockout Battle (ノックアウトバトル) at Pokémon Battle Tour 09, played with 60-card decks; those winners got this gold Victory Medal, showing Arceus, together with the silver one, 036/DPt-P, while three straight wins in the half league, with 30-card decks, brought only the silver. Pokémon Battle Tour 09 (ポケモンバトルツアー09) was the big Pokémon event of summer 2009, held at shops across Japan, mostly AEON group stores, on one day each between 11 July and 6 September 2009, in place of the Battle Road tournaments of earlier summers. It offered card battles, a beginners' class, a lottery and a chance to try the new Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver games. Everyone who took part got Mewtwo 049/DPt-P.

Yusuke Ishikawa drew it.
